title: `scan_deps()` seems to fail when the input path is a file (not folder)
description:
`scan_deps()` seems to fail if the path input is a file rather than a folder.

This fails:

``` r
dir.create(f <- tempfile())
od <- setwd(f)
tryCatch(
    finally = {
        setwd(od)
        unlink(f, recursive = TRUE)
    }, 
    expr = {
        cat("dplyr::filter(mtcars, cyl == 4)\n", file = "example.R")
        pkgdepends::scan_deps("example.R", root = ".")    
    }
)
#> Error in `writeLines()`:
#> ! can only write character objects

```

This works:

```r
dir.create(f <- tempfile())
od <- setwd(f)
tryCatch(
    finally = {
        setwd(od)
        unlink(f, recursive = TRUE)
    }, 
    expr = {
        dir.create("folder")
        cat("dplyr::filter(mtcars, cyl == 4)\n", file = "folder/example.R")
        pkgdepends::scan_deps("folder", root = ".")    
    }
)
#> 
#> Dependencies:
#> + dplyr @ example.R
```

title: pkgdepends (and pak) fail when GitHub packages depend on each other and different versions are requested
description:
I noticed that pkgdepends fails to resolve multiple github packages that depend on each other:
A reprex:

on d59d4ee3b702d3ff2a38450ace2ae3050d17fc35 I get:
```r
obj <- pkgdepends::new_pkg_deps(c(
  pkgdepends = "r-lib/pkgdepends@d59d4ee3b702d3ff2a38450ace2ae3050d17fc35",
  pkgcache   = "r-lib/pkgcache@93010c2f496705395f70c284c8925fe72bc092f3"
))

sol <- obj$solve()$get_solution()
print(sol)
```
gives output:
```r
<pkg_solution>
+ result: FAILED
+ refs:
  - r-lib/pkgcache@93010c2f496705395f70c284c8925fe72bc092f3
  - r-lib/pkgdepends@d59d4ee3b702d3ff2a38450ace2ae3050d17fc35
+ constraints (62):
  - select pkgdepends exactly once
  - select pkgcache exactly once
  - select callr at most once
  - select cli at most once
  - select curl at most once
  - select desc at most once
  - select filelock at most once
  - select jsonlite at most once
  - select lpSolve at most once
  - select otel at most once
  ...
x failures:
* r-lib/pkgdepends@d59d4ee3b702d3ff2a38450ace2ae3050d17fc35: Can't install dependency r-lib/pkgcache@feature/ppm-sso (>= 2.2.0)
* r-lib/pkgcache@feature/ppm-sso: Conflicts with r-lib/pkgcache@93010c2f496705395f70c284c8925fe72bc092f3
```
there appears to be a conflict with the remote from the DESCRIPTION `r-lib/pkgcache@feature/ppm-sso` and the explicitly requested `r-lib/pkgcache@93010c2f496705395f70c284c8925fe72bc092f3`. This also happens when there are no branches listed, e.g., `Remotes: r-lib/pkgcache` would have also errored.

Originally observed when using `renv` to restore a lockfile using pak on CI, which failed to resolve the dependencies. This behavior appears to be in pkgdepends already since v0.8.0 (or earlier, I didn't test that far back). Perhaps this is intended, but it does complicate reproducibility. Note that the error did not surface with `pak` 0.9.5, only since 0.10.0. Still, this felt like the right place for the issue.

title: `lockfile_install()` reinstalls source packages every time when CRAN is cran.r-universe.dev
description:
I noticed this on cmdstanr's windows-11-arm GitHub Actions job, where setup-r-dependencies restores a 93 MB library from the cache and then `pak::lockfile_install()` rebuilds the whole thing from source anyway ("Will install 91 packages", "added 90, dld 90", about 26 minutes). The same workflow on windows-latest says "kept 86, added 3" and is done in 20 seconds. See https://github.com/stan-dev/cmdstanr/actions/runs/37052454400/job/110988918897 setup-r-dependencies step.

I did some digging (Claude assisted) and I think this is because the R build that setup-r installs on Windows ARM sets CRAN to https://cran.r-universe.dev. With pak 0.11.1 every entry in our lockfile is "platform": "source", "repotype": "cran", and `installedok_remote_cran()` requires

```
    identical(installed[["repository"]], "CRAN")
```

But source tarballs from r-universe use `Repository: https://cran.r-universe.dev` in DESCRIPTION, and `add_metadata()` writes the Remote* fields but doesn't touch Repository, so nothing pak installed from r-universe can pass the check and `pkgplan_update()` just reinstalls everything on every run.

I asked Claude to come up with this minimal reproducible example (I see the same thing with pak 0.9.2 and 0.11.1.9000):

```r
    Sys.setenv(PKG_PLATFORMS = "source")
    options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cran.r-universe.dev"))
    lib <- tempfile(); dir.create(lib)
    pak::lockfile_create("abind", lockfile = "pkg.lock", lib = NULL)
    pak::lockfile_install("pkg.lock", lib = lib)  # added 1
    pak::lockfile_install("pkg.lock", lib = lib)  # added 1 again
    packageDescription("abind", lib.loc = lib)$Repository
    #> "https://cran.r-universe.dev"
```

If `repos` is set to `c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org")` the second call says "kept 1" and Repository is "CRAN".

Would a solution be for the source branch to also accept a package whose RemoteRepos matches the lockfile entry, the way `installedok_remote_standard()` does for source packages from other repos? pak writes RemoteRepos at install time, so anything pak installed would pass.

title: Support zstd-compressed package archives: CRAN's current macOS binaries fail with "unknown archive type"
description:
## Request

Please recognize zstd-compressed tarballs in `detect_package_archive_type()`.
CRAN's macOS builder has started compressing `.tgz` binaries with zstd, and pkgdepends rejects those archives before extraction, so pak cannot install affected packages on macOS at all.

I searched the pkgdepends and pak issues, pull requests and commit history for `zstd`, `unknown archive type`, and macOS binary compression, and found no existing report or pending fix.

## Discovery context

A package's GitHub Actions matrix started failing on 2026-09-20 in the macOS job, during dependency installation, while the commit under test changed only documentation. Linux and Windows passed on the same commit, and the same macOS job had passed on the previous commit the day before:

```
✔ Got knitr 1.52 (aarch64-apple-darwin23) (992.43 kB)
Error:
! error in pak subprocess
Caused by error in `make_install_process(filename, lib = lib, metadata = metadata)`:
! Cannot extract
'/var/folders/.../bin/macosx/sonoma-arm64/contrib/4.6/knitr_1.52.tgz',
unknown archive type.
```

Full log: https://github.com/RGenomicsETL/CanardAbsurd/actions/runs/35490731798/job/106025966856

The reported 992.43 kB did not match the 1,077,421 bytes the same file has on Posit Package Manager, which first looked like a truncated download. 

Clearing the runner caches and re-running three times reproduced it exactly, and fetching CRAN's copy directly showed the difference is the compression format, not a corrupt transfer.

## Reproduction

This needs no macOS runner; the detection is pure R. On Linux, R 4.6.0,
pkgdepends 0.9.1:

```r
url <- "https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/macosx/sonoma-arm64/contrib/4.6/knitr_1.52.tgz"
download.file(url, f <- tempfile(fileext = ".tgz"), mode = "wb")

readBin(f, "raw", 4)
#> [1] 28 b5 2f fd                      # zstd magic

untar(f, list = TRUE)[1:3]
#> [1] "knitr/" "knitr/CITATION" "knitr/misc/"    # base R reads it

pkgdepends:::detect_package_archive_type(f)
#> [1] "unknown"
```

`untar()` lists the archive with both `tar = "internal"` and the external tar,
so R itself handles these files.

## What CRAN now serves

Sampled from `bin/macosx/sonoma-arm64/contrib/4.6/` on cloud.r-project.org:

| Package | First bytes | Compression | Size |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|
| knitr 1.52 | `28 b5 2f fd` | zstd | 992,429 |
| xfun 0.61 | `28 b5 2f fd` | zstd | 656,512 |
| cli 3.6.6 | `1f 8b 08 00` | gzip | 1,487,045 |
| jsonlite 2.0.0 | `1f 8b 08 00` | gzip | 1,112,267 |
| evaluate 1.0.5 | `1f 8b 08 00` | gzip | 103,958 |

Recently built packages are zstd and older ones are still gzip, so this should
spread as CRAN rebuilds. Posit Package Manager still publishes gzip builds of
the same versions (`knitr_1.52.tgz` is 1,077,421 bytes there), which is why the
failure depends on which repository a runner resolves.

## Where it fails

`detect_package_archive_type()` in `R/install-tar.R` tests only gzip, zip,
bzip2 and xz magic bytes and returns `"unknown"` otherwise. `R/install-binary.R`
then throws `install_input_error` rather than extracting.

## Suggested direction

Detecting the zstd magic `28 b5 2f fd` looks sufficient for the tar path: the
compression-flag helper already returns no flag for types it does not name, and
macOS `tar` is bsdtar/libarchive, which detects compression itself. GNU tar
would need `--zstd`, and a build of tar without zstd support would still fail,
so the error may be worth keeping for that case. I have not written or tested a
patch.

## Workaround, for anyone hitting this in CI

`r-lib/actions/setup-r` routes macOS through Posit Package Manager only for a
fixed list of repository owners unless `use-public-rspm: always` is set. Setting
it restores gzip binaries and made our matrix green again. That depends on Posit
Package Manager keeping gzip, so it is a stopgap rather than a fix.

## Environment

- Failure: GitHub Actions `macos-latest` (macOS Tahoe 26.6.2), aarch64-apple-darwin23,
  R 4.6.1 (2026-06-24), pak 0.11.1 via `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies`.
- Reproduction above: Linux x86_64, R 4.6.0 (2026-04-24), pkgdepends 0.9.1.

## Limits

I have not established when CRAN changed compression or which builder made the
change, and I sampled five packages rather than surveying the repository.
Windows binaries are `.zip` and source installs are unaffected. I have not
checked whether other consumers of these archives, such as renv or
`install.packages()` with a custom method, are affected.

---
Prepared with Claude Opus 5 in Claude Code.

title: Vendored git-auth.R will need a re-vendor if gitcreds renames the cache env var
description:
`R/git-auth.R` is a vendored copy of the gitcreds standalone file. Line 219 computes the cache
environment variable name:

```r
paste0("GITHUB_PAT_", toupper(slug3))
```

There are open PRs on gitcreds to move that prefix to `GITCREDS_PAT_`: r-lib/gitcreds#76, r-lib/gitcreds#77 and r-lib/gitcreds#78, for r-lib/gitcreds#56. Filing here so the re-vendor is on the radar. 

One specific to pkgdepends: `git_creds_for_url()` writes `"FAIL"` to the computed name as a
negative cache, and gitcreds honors that sentinel by throwing before it asks git. So the variable
is a channel between the two copies, not just a user-facing string. r-lib/gitcreds#77 deliberately scopes
the sentinel to the canonical name, because honoring it under legacy names too would let a
`FAIL` written here suppress a credential that is present:

```r
library(gitcreds)

cfg <- tempfile()
writeLines(c(
  "[credential]",
  "\thelper = \"!f() { test \\\"$1\\\" = get && echo username=demo-user && echo password=real-token; }; f\""
), cfg)

url <- "https://gitlab.example.com"
ev  <- gitcreds_cache_envvar(url)   #> "GITHUB_PAT_GITLAB_EXAMPLE_COM"

withr::with_envvar(c(GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL = cfg, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM = "1"), {
  gitcreds_get(url, use_cache = FALSE, set_cache = FALSE)$username
  #> [1] "demo-user"                      # the store has a good credential

  withr::with_envvar(structure(list("FAIL"), names = ev), gitcreds_get(url))
  #> Error: Could not find any credentials
})
```

Worth noting that pak ships pkgdepends in a pinned private library, so the skew between the two
copies outlives a gitcreds upgrade in the user's own library.

title: `git::` remote installs silently deliver Git LFS pointer files instead of the real file content, with no error or warning
description:
## Description

When installing an R package from a `git::` remote (via `pak::pak()` / `pkg_install()`) whose repository tracks one or more files with **Git LFS** (`.gitattributes` with a `filter=lfs` entry), the installed package ends up with the raw ~130-byte **LFS pointer text file** (e.g. `version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1\noid sha256:...\nsize ...`) in place of the real file content — and `pak::pak()` reports a normal, successful install, with no warning or error about it.

This happens **regardless of whether `git-lfs` is installed and initialized on the machine** (`git lfs install` run beforehand makes no difference). We confirmed this is because pkgdepends' `git::` remote handler uses its **own built-in git client** rather than shelling out to the system `git` binary (per the pkgdepends docs: "does not require a system Git installation"). Git LFS is implemented as an external filter (`clean`/`smudge`) that only the real `git` CLI invokes during checkout, driven by config that `git lfs install` writes to `.gitconfig`, and by the `git-lfs` binary itself acting as a filter subprocess. A built-in git client that never shells out to `git`/`git-lfs` structurally cannot trigger that filter — so LFS content can never be resolved via this path today, silently.

## Reprex

I can't share our internal repo/host, but this reproduces unmodified against a disposable **gitlab.com** (or github.com) repo:

### Setup (one-time)

1. Create a throwaway repo, e.g. `youruser/lfstest`, with a minimal valid `DESCRIPTION` at its root (a trivial R package is enough for `pak` to resolve it).
2. Track a file with Git LFS and commit/push it:
   ```bash
   git lfs install
   git lfs track "inst/bin/payload"
   git add .gitattributes
   head -c 1000000 /dev/urandom > inst/bin/payload   # anything non-trivial in size
   git add inst/bin/payload DESCRIPTION
   git commit -m "add lfs-tracked payload"
   git push
   ```

### Failing case — `pak::pak()`, even with git-lfs installed

```bash
# git-lfs IS installed and initialized on this machine -- doesn't matter
git lfs install
Rscript -e 'pak::pak("git::https://gitlab.com/youruser/lfstest.git")'
```

```r
# after install, inspect what actually landed:
p <- system.file("bin", "payload", package = "lfstest")
file.size(p)                                    # ~130, not ~1000000
readLines(p, n = 1)                              # "version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1"
```

`pak::pak()` exits 0 / reports success. No warning is printed about `payload` being unresolved LFS content.

### Non-failing case — a real `git clone` of the same repo, same machine

```bash
git clone https://gitlab.com/youruser/lfstest.git /tmp/lfstest_check
file.size("/tmp/lfstest_check/inst/bin/payload")  # ~1000000, correct
```

Same machine, same `git-lfs` install, same credentials — a real `git clone` resolves the LFS content correctly; `pak::pak()` on the identical URL does not.

## Expected vs actual behavior

**Expected:** either (a) `git::` remote installs resolve Git LFS pointers to their real content (e.g. via the LFS batch API, which is plain HTTPS and wouldn't require shelling out to the `git-lfs` binary), or, at minimum, (b) `pak::pak()`/`pkgdepends` detects that a required file is an LFS pointer (or that the repo's `.gitattributes` declares LFS filters) and **fails loudly** with a clear message, instead of completing the install "successfully" with corrupted content.

**Actual:** the install silently succeeds and leaves LFS-tracked files as unresolved pointer text, with no indication anything is wrong. This is a correctness footgun: it fails exactly where a user is least likely to notice (a large binary silently becoming a 130-byte text file), and can go unnoticed until whatever consumes that file crashes or misbehaves much later, in an unrelated part of a pipeline.

## Environment

- R version: 4.5.x
- pak: latest stable, installed via the official binary channel (`https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/...`)
- OS: a recent `rocker/r-ver`-based Debian/Ubuntu Docker image (also reproduces outside Docker)
- `git-lfs`: tested both absent and present/initialized (`git lfs install`) — no difference in outcome
- Git host: a self-hosted GitLab instance internally; expected (and structurally should, given the built-in-git-client explanation above) to reproduce identically against gitlab.com/github.com per the reprex

## Additional context

Searched the `r-lib/pkgdepends` and `r-lib/pak` issue trackers for "lfs" before filing and found no existing reports of this.

I understand full LFS support is a larger ask; even just surfacing a warning/error when a pulled file turns out to be an LFS pointer (the pointer format is trivially detectable: a small text file starting with `version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1`) would turn this from a silent data-corruption trap into a clear, actionable failure.

title: .Rbuildignore with conditional inclusions breaks submodule handling
description:
I've hit a little bit of an edge-case with the `.Rbuildignore` & submodule interaction. My [package](https://github.com/andrjohns/newstan) uses the `.Rbuildignore` to only retain a [subset of folders/files from submodules](https://github.com/andrjohns/newstan/blob/main/.Rbuildignore) when packaging:

```gitignore
^src/stan/(?!(src$|src/stan))
^src/math/(?!(stan|lib$|lib/opencl_([^\/]*)|lib/sundials_([^\/]*)$|lib/sundials_([^\/]*)/src|lib/sundials_([^\/]*)/include))
```

title: Allow trailing slash(es) in urls?
description:
Could the regex matching be extended to allow trailing slash(es) in urls? I.e. allow `https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/` as a valid url.

title: feature request: auto-detect R package in well-known subdirectories
description:
### Motivation

  Multi-language repositories are becoming more common within the Shiny team - a single repo may contain a Python package, a
  JavaScript frontend, and an R package, each in their own subdirectory. Today, installing the R package from
   such a repo requires explicitly specifying `subdir`:

  ```r
  pak::pkg_install("owner/repo/pkg-r")
  ```

  This works, but it requires the caller to know ahead of time where the R package lives. It also makes it
  impossible for package authors to establish a convention that "just works" for users installing with `pak`.

  ### Proposed behaviour

  When a GitHub (or Git) remote is resolved and no `subdir` is specified, and no `DESCRIPTION` is found at
  the repo root, automatically probe a list of well-known subdirectory candidates before failing with a "no
  package" error.

  A reasonable default probe list might be:

  ```
  pkg-r/
  r/
  ```

  The first subdirectory containing a valid `DESCRIPTION` file would be used automatically.

  ### Current behaviour

  In `type-github.R`, [`type_github_get_data_ref()`](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/blob/634661a7d91b41476fd1ab653fe3087a6e40b8a9/R/type-github.R#L301-L336) constructs a GraphQL query that looks for `DESCRIPTION` at
   exactly `{subdir}DESCRIPTION`. If `subdir` is empty (not specified) and no `DESCRIPTION` exists at the
  root, `check_github_response_ref()` throws a `new_github_no_package_error`. There is no fallback probing.

  ### Implementation sketch

  The probing could be done by:

  1. Issuing a single GraphQL query that requests `DESCRIPTION` at multiple paths in one round-trip (GraphQL
  aliases make this straightforward).
  2. If the root `DESCRIPTION` is `null`, iterating through the alias results to find the first non-null hit
  and using that `subdir` for the remainder of resolution.

  This avoids additional HTTP round-trips and keeps the change self-contained in `type_github_get_data_ref()`
   (and the equivalent `_pull`/`_sha` variants).

  ### Notes

  - This would be opt-in via convention — repos that have a `DESCRIPTION` at the root are unaffected.
  - The probe list could be configurable (e.g., via a `pak` option or a `DESCRIPTION`-adjacent marker file),
  but a sensible hardcoded default would cover the majority of cases.
  - Related: r-lib/pak#646 (explicit `subdir` for `git::` remotes — a complementary but separate issue).

title: Potential bug: Passing install_args to package building is overwritten when detecting multiarch
description:
When creating the install plan, the code currently overwrites any values stored in install_args to either be an empty string or "--no-multiarch". 

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/blob/d59d4ee3b702d3ff2a38450ace2ae3050d17fc35/R/solve.R#L1382

I would like to propose that instead of overwriting it, adding it to the list of arguments to be passed on when building/installing the packages.

This is related to #394, as but I was seeing if I could modify the lock file to do what I wanted.

example lockfile:

```
{
  "lockfile_version": 1,

title: test-coverage workflow fails on fork PRs: fake GitHub server returns HTTP 401 in github-tools tests
description:
## Summary

The `test-coverage` workflow (`uncovr::test()`) fails on pull requests **from forks**. Every test in `tests/testthat/test-github-tools.R` errors or fails because the in-process fake GitHub GraphQL server (`gh_app()` in `R/gh-app.R`) responds with **HTTP 401 "Bad credentials"** — i.e. the `Authorization` header produced by `type_github_get_headers()` does not satisfy `re_gh_auth()` in that job's environment.

First observed on the `test-coverage` job of #466 (a fork PR). It is **not** caused by that PR — see "Why this is independent" below.

## Symptoms (from the failing run)

- First failure is an **error**, not a snapshot diff:
  - `Error ('test-github-tools.R:4:3'): type_github_get_data, sha, description`
  - `! Bad GitHub credentials, make sure that your GitHub token is valid.`
  - `Caused by error in stop(http_error(resp)): Unauthorized (HTTP 401).`
  - The request URL in the condition is the **local** fake server (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>//graphql`), so this is the fake server's auth middleware rejecting the token, not real GitHub.
- All remaining `github-tools` failures are snapshot mismatches that are **downstream** of that 401 (each now contains an extra `+ Caused by error in stop(http_error(resp))` line).
- Net: `github-tools` reports ~15 failures; the job exits non-zero.

Failing run: https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/actions/runs/26966219572/job/79569428678

## What passes (scoping)

- All `R-CMD-check` matrix jobs (macOS / Ubuntu / Windows, release + oldrels) on the **same fork PR** — `github-tools` passes there.
- `test-coverage` on `main` **push** events (e.g. the 2026-06-01 run).
- `uncovr::test()` **locally** — `github-tools` passes; only unrelated environmental failures occur (`test-assertions`, `type-standard`/`type-bioc` new-R snapshots, `scan-deps` tempdir).

So the failure is specific to **`test-coverage` (uncovr/covr) + fork-PR** environment. Both `R-CMD-check.yaml` and `test-coverage.yaml` set the identical `GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`, so the differentiator is the coverage harness, not the token env declaration alone. This is the first fork PR to trigger `test-coverage` (the workflow was added 2026-05-21), which is why it has not surfaced before.

## Likely area

`type_github_get_headers()` (`R/type-github.R`) selects a token (`CI_GITHUB_TOKEN` → `gitcreds_get()` → bundled PAT), and the fake server's auth middleware in `gh_app()` rejects it via `re_gh_auth()` (`^token (gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{36,251}|[[:xdigit:]]{40})$`). In the fork-PR coverage environment the resulting `Authorization` value evidently doesn't match. Needs reproduction in that specific environment to confirm the exact token value.

## Possible fixes (for a follow-up PR)

- Set `CI_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` in `test-coverage.yaml` (so a known-good token is used), or
- Make the fake server's auth check tolerant of the token form seen in this environment, or
- Skip the auth check / `github-tools` snapshot tests when no usable token is available.

## Why this is independent of #466

#466 does not modify the auth middleware, `re_gh_auth()`, `type_github_get_headers()`, the token-selection path, or the `github-tools` tests. Its only `github-tools` change is the snapshot file, which is compared *after* the (failing) request, so it cannot cause a 401.

title: Bug: Cached zip treated as valid but yields empty archive on install
description:
## Bug: Cached zip treated as valid but yields empty archive on install

**Labels:** bug, cache

### Description

When installing packages via `pak::pak()`, a cached `.zip` that pak reports as valid ("Cached copy … is the latest build") is later found to be an empty archive during extraction, causing a hard error. The cache lookup succeeds but the cached file is corrupt/empty, so no download is attempted and installation fails.

### Steps to reproduce

```r
pak::pak(c('jsonlite', 'rlang'))
```

### Expected behavior

Either the cached file is validated before skipping the download (and re-downloaded if corrupt), or the error is caught and pak falls back to a fresh download automatically.

### Actual behavior

pak reports the cache is fresh and skips the download, then fails during extraction with:

```
! C:\Users\…\jsonlite_2.0.0.zip is not a valid R package, it is an empty archive.
```

### Error output

```
Error: 
! error in pak subprocess
Caused by error in `verify_extracted_package(filename, pkg_cache)`:
! C:\Users\tus75918\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpovMw7R\file431c6a465617/bin/windows/contrib/4.6/jsonlite_2.0.0.zip is not a valid R package, it is an empty archive.

Subprocess backtrace:
 1. base::withCallingHandlers(...)
 2. get("pkg_install_do_plan", asNamespace("pak"))(...)
 3. proposal$install()
 4. pkgdepends::install_package_plan(...)
 5. base::withCallingHandlers({...})
 6. pkgdepends:::handle_events(state, events)
 7. pkgdepends:::handle_event(state, i)
 8. proc$get_result()
 9. processx:::process_get_result(self, private)
10. private$post_process()
11. pkgdepends:::install_extracted_binary(...)
12. pkgdepends:::verify_extracted_package(filename, pkg_cache)
13. base::throw(...)
```

### Environment

- **Platform:** Windows (x86_64-w64-mingw32)  
- **R version:** 4.6.x (inferred from contrib path)  
- **Packages affected:** jsonlite 2.0.0, rlang 1.2.0  
- **Cache path:** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\RtmpovMw7R\`

### Suggested fix

In `pkgdepends:::install_extracted_binary` (or the cache-hit logic upstream), validate that the cached zip is non-empty and well-formed _before_ deciding to skip the download. If validation fails, evict the entry from the cache and re-download.

title: Setting command line arguments for package installation
description:
I opened this issue in {pak} before, but I think it is better addressed in {pkgdepends}. Here is the link to the original issue  https://github.com/r-lib/pak/issues/514.

I would like to test installed packages using `tools::testInstalledPackage()`, see https://rdrr.io/r/tools/testInstalledPackage.html.

In order to run all R code in the examples, tests, and vignettes, examples and tests need to be explicitly installed during installation. For examples this is the default, for tests not. 

In order to do that, one would have to set `R CMD INSTALL --install-tests` as installation command line argument. 

I am not sure how to set command line arguments in a package installation plan. 

It seems that this might already be possible, see the `cmd_args` argument in `make_build_process()` https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/blob/6741f04bf5f7fc8d73d87b3a326b1bf5a3914a38/R/install-plan.R#L356-L357 but it is unlcear to me how to pass it from a package installation proposal since there is not configuation option matching the argument.

title: Local installs vs. GH dependencies
description:
Currently if a dependency is from GH via `Remotes` (or any way, really?), and there is a locally installed package, pak will always update that package from GH. I _think_ this is because
1. It is hard to say what the user really wants, and after all the user said they wanted that package from GH.
2. It is not possible to determine the relationship between the installed package and the package in the GH repo.

Which all makes sense to me, but it also makes local development cumbersome when you are working on two packages locally and one depends on the other one.

This also happens in Positron, which uses `local_install*()` (?).

Btw. this is not unique to `github::`, but applies to all other remote types (git, gitlab, url, etc. possibly even standard, cran, bioc.)

title: Dependency scanning: ability to declare non-cran dependency
description:
It would be nice to be able to declare a non-cran dependency, in a way that is detected by `dependencies()`, without creating a full `DESCRIPTION` file.

One way would be to put something like
```r
# pak::pak("user/repo@branch")
library(repo)
```
into a `deps.R` file. AFAIK people already use these files as a convention to declare undetected CRAN(-like) dependencies, so this would be a natural addition.

We could also have an alternative syntax with `renv::install(...)` instead of the `pak()` call.

Similar issue in renv: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/2094

title: `sysreqs_install_plan` outputs partial dependency list for some platforms (with no warning)
description:
Here, "partially-supported platforms" appears to include supported OSs with versions that aren't in `pak:::supported_os_versions()` and OSs with an unsupported `distribution` (e.g., opensuse-tumbleweed) that, due to a very particular prefix, seems to end up being treated the same way.

``` r
pkgdepends::sysreqs_install_plan(
              "sf",
              config = list(sysreqs_platform = "opensuse-42.3")
            )$packages$sysreq # includes proj sysreq --- the correct result
#> ℹ Loading metadata database
#> ✔ Loading metadata database ... done
#> 
#> [1] "gdal"    "geos"    "openssl" "proj"    "sqlite3"
pkgdepends::sysreqs_install_plan(
  "sf",
  config = list(sysreqs_platform = "opensuse-42.2")
)$packages$sysreq # excludes proj sysreq
#> [1] "gdal"    "geos"    "openssl" "sqlite3"
pkgdepends::sysreqs_install_plan(
  "sf",
  config = list(sysreqs_platform = "opensuse-tumbleweed-20240809")
)$packages$sysreq # aborts (but this doesn't seem to be what is used downstream)
#> Error in "sysreqs2_command(sysreqs_platform, \"update\")": ! Unknown OS. Don't know how to query or install system packages for
#> opensuse-tumbleweed-20240809.
pkgdepends::sysreqs_install_plan(
  "sf",
  config = list(sysreqs_platform = "x86_64-suse-linux-gnu-opensuse-tumbleweed-20240809")
)$packages$sysreq # excludes proj sysreq
#> [1] "gdal"    "geos"    "openssl" "sqlite3"

# extra setup info:
options("repos") # RSPM + CRAN; same sorts of things appear to happen also with CRAN only
#> $repos
#>                                            RSPM 
#> "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/all/latest" 
#>                                            CRAN 
#>                     "https://cran.rstudio.com/"
pkgdepends::current_r_platform()
#> [1] "x86_64-suse-linux-gnu-opensuse-tumbleweed-20240809"
pkgdepends::sysreqs_platforms()[9,] # opensuse-* --- but not all opensuse versions are fully supported
#> # A data frame: 1 × 7
#>   name   os    distribution version update_command install_command query_command
#> * <chr>  <chr> <chr>        <chr>   <chr>          <chr>           <chr>        
#> 1 openS… linux opensuse     *       <NA>           zypper --non-i… rpm
pak:::supported_os_versions()$opensuse
#> [1] "42.3" "15.0"
pkgdepends::sysreqs_is_supported("opensuse-42.3") # "full" support
#> [1] TRUE
pkgdepends::sysreqs_is_supported("opensuse-42.2") # but actually has "partial" support
#> [1] TRUE
pkgdepends::sysreqs_is_supported("opensuse-tumbleweed-20240809") # unsupported, but this isn't what `pak` tries
#> [1] FALSE
pkgdepends::sysreqs_is_supported("x86_64-suse-linux-gnu-opensuse-tumbleweed-20240809") # but actually has "partial" support
#> [1] TRUE
```

<sup>Created on 2024-08-13 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

[See also [this comment](https://github.com/r-lib/pak/issues/610#issuecomment-2074887377) for what looks like another downstream example involving redhat & units.  I think this comment and my example above form a separate issue from pak#610 itself.]

## Context

I was trying `pak::pkg_install("sf")` on OpenSUSE Tumbleweed, which fails with suboptimal feedback.  (This could be improved downstream in `pak` by displaying or pointing to `.Last.error$parent${stdout,stderr}` rather than just `.Last.error`; in this case, `stdout` shows that there's an issue with using PROJ.  But it seems that there's still something going amiss in `pkgdepends` underneath this.)

I'm not sure whether this is an instance of #320.  I got the impression that it wasn't since it appeared to happen with both CRAN and CRAN+RSPM as `repos`, as well as both before and after successfully installing sf (with PROJ and other sysreqs).

## Desired behavior

`sysreqs_install_plan`, when the platform isn't fully supported, will do one of the following:
- Explanatory hard error, potentially pointing to a hack like `Sys.setenv("PKG_SYSREQS_PLATFORM" = "opensuse-42.3")`
- Explanatory warning + current result
- Explanatory warning + use something like hack above, trying to grab dependency info from a fully-supported version

Hopefully, any of these would at least attach some additional useful context when things go wrong downstream, like in `pak::pkg_install("sf")` [though I haven't confirmed warnings/errors wouldn't somehow be swallowed and hidden away by `pak`].

title: Automatically `normalizePath()` for local type of references
description:
Given the following file structure:
```
my_packages/
├── pkg1
├── pkg2
├── pkg3
└── ...
```
I usually do:
```
setwd("my_packages/pkg1")
```
And then want to do the following:
```
pak::pak("../pkg2")
```
But it results in the following error:
```
Error: 
! error in pak subprocess
Caused by error in `get_remote_types(refs)`:
! Cannot parse package:
../pkg2.
ℹ See `?pkgdepends::pkg_refs()` for supported
  package sources.
Type .Last.error to see the more details.
```

The solution is to convert the path to be in absolute form via `normalizePath()`. This is definitely not the end of the world but involves a lot of typing given how short&sweet the `pak::pak()` command is.

My request is: can it be done automatically (for all local type of reference)?

title: Error message in case of circular dependencies
description:
This is a duplicate of #357 (with a different scope for a possible "fix"):

Having two packages (A and B) directly depend on each other, as part of a call to `pak::lockfile_install()`, will generate an error as

```
Error: 
! error in pak subprocess
Caused by error in `select_next_task(state)`:
! Cannot select new package installation task.
ℹ 2 packages still waiting to install: A and B.
ℹ This is an internal error in pkgdepends, please report an issue at
  <https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/issues>.
``` 

Ofc this is a "user error". Nevertheless: a more specific error msg could very much help getting to the underlying issue quicker.

The same issue also came up in #306, where a more telling error message could have been helpful as well.

(I am opening this here even though the problem came up with pak, on account of clear directions to do so in the mentioned error msg.)

title: binary packages install are failing when download method gets source
description:
`ip$install()` call fails on verifying the binary package after the installation proposal download call (see below for an example)
  - Fail is random, as it may use the `resolution$sources` item that is not `Archive` most of the time
  - Fail sometimes happens if non-archive source is downloaded
    - can be mitigated with another download

This was detected when installing `insightsengineering/teal.modules.clinical` with 2 problematic binary packages `nloptr` and `urltools` (using ppm snapshot or latest).

- ~Is there an option to disable resolving the `Archive` URL?~
  - doesn't happen only on Archive URL (however, this one always downloads source packages)
- Could the method fall back to installing a source package or re-downloading again?

#### Reproducible example

note: I think this results from a race condition when downloading the file with `pkgcache::download_one_of(...)` and it downloads a source archive.

```R
config <- list(
  cran_mirror = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/noble/2024-04-19", 
  library = tempfile()
)

ip <- pkgdepends::new_pkg_installation_proposal("tern", config = config)

ip$solve()

res <- ip$get_resolution()

# Keep only Archive sources (force failure)
new_sources <- lapply(
  res$sources,
  function(x) {
    if (length(x) > 1 && any(grepl("src/contrib/Archive", x))) {
      x[grepl("src/contrib/Archive", x)]
    } else {
      x
    }
  }
)

ip$.__enclos_env__$private$plan$.__enclos_env__$private$resolution$result$sources <- new_sources

ip$download()
ip$install()
```

title: Warning in cond$parent: partial match of 'parent' to 'parents'

title: pkgdepends fails to download from private git url, despite successfully resolving dependencies
description:
I tried my best to track this issue down, but it's been a bit tricky to navigate the `pak` private library and async. Hopefully I'm close enough that the bug report is useful. 

### Reproducing the error

I'm struggling to find a way to make a full reprex, but the situation is

* Enterprise GitLab
* Using username and access token configured via `gitcreds`

```r
spec <- "pkgname=git::https://enterprise.com/org/pkgname.git"
prop <- pkgdepends::new_pkg_installation_proposal(spec)
prop$download()
# ℹ Getting 13 pkgs with unknown sizes
# ✖ Failed to download pkgname 0.0.0.9000 (source)
# ✔ Cached copy of RColorBrewer 1.1-3 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-ubuntu-22.04) is the latest build
# ✔ Cached copy of colorspace 2.1-0 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-ubuntu-22.04) is the latest build
# ✔ Cached copy of farver 2.1.1 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-ubuntu-22.04) is the latest build
# ...
# ✖ Failed to download 1 package. 
```

### Best effort at debugging

Given the remote, 
* I've successfully fetched the `DESCRIPTION` info using [`pkgdepends:::type_git_get_data(remote)`](https://github.com/r-lib/pak/blob/a31499906ff4f994a789e7a0ee000da29a790ba3/src/library/pkgdepends/R/type-git.R#L21)
* But then I hit an error at [`async_git_download_repo(url, ref = sha, output = pkgdir)`](https://github.com/r-lib/pak/blob/a31499906ff4f994a789e7a0ee000da29a790ba3/src/library/pkgdepends/R/type-git.R#L95) (or `git_download_repo`)
  ```r
  pkgdepends:::synchronize(pkgdepends:::async_git_download_repo(url, ref = sha, output = "/tmp/pkgname"))
  # Error in writeBin(parsed[[tr$hash[l]]]$raw, opath) : 
  #   can only write vector objects
  ```
 
> [!NOTE] 
> while exploring this, [this line seems like it's improperly indexed](https://github.com/r-lib/pak/blob/a31499906ff4f994a789e7a0ee000da29a790ba3/src/library/pkgdepends/R/type-git.R#L92C1-L92C49) and I had to make the following modification just to attempt a download:
> ```diff
> - sha <- resolution$metadata[[1]][["RemoteSha"]]
> + sha <- resolution$metadata[["RemoteSha"]]
> ```

title: Typo when checking for truthy strings
description:
I think there is a typo in this code:
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/blob/a89923be1648716d8e1c3e8c56421353d72e33ff/R/utils.R#L518C1-L523C2

The variable "thruthy" should be "truthy":
```
# Incorrect
thruthy_strings <- c("true", "t", "1", "on", "yes", "on")
# Correct
truthy_strings <- c("true", "t", "1", "on", "yes", "on")

So that the function works (which uses `truthy_strings`):
```
is_truthy <- function(x) {
  (is.logical(x) && length(x) >= 1 && !is.na(x[[1]]) && x[[1]]) ||
    (is.character(x) && length(x) >= 1 && tolower(x) %in% truthy_strings)
}

title: How to get the original R_LIBRARY_DIR from configure script
description:
In the "staged install" of `R CMD INSTALL`, the environment variable `${R_PACKAGE_DIR}` holds a temporary directory, which differs from the actual target directory, `${R_LIBRARY_DIR}/${R_PACKAGE_NAME}`. That is OK. I am developing a couple of packages with `configure` scripts using these environment variables, and they work fine with `R CMD check` and `devtools::install_github()`.

I tried replacing `devtools::install_github()` with `pak::pkg_install()`, but it did not work presumably because `.libPaths()` is modified, and `${R_LIBRARY_DIR}` holds a temporary directory instead of the actual library path.
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/blob/0807835e65027bcdb4dd9ff53dade85d3f81a351/R/install-plan.R#L393-L399

Is there any way to avoid `.libPaths()` modification, or to get the original `${R_LIBRARY_DIR}` from the `configure` script executed in a subprocess?

title: Rmd YAML header?
description:
This is pretty difficult, unfortunately, but could not come up with a
simpler solution.

* We use tree-sitter to parse and search the YAML, so that we can have
  coordinates, and also the search is much simpler than when using a YAML
  parser.
* The tree-sitter parser cannot scan the actual values of the scalars, so
  we use a YAML parser for that (libyaml). (No, it is not better to scan
  them manually, they are quite involved.)
* Scanning the scalars is a transformation, not just a subsetting, so
  we lose the correct coordinates for the things (e.g. R code) _within_
  the values. We still have the coordinates for the values, though.
* We don't handle references correctly, because the tree-sitter parser
  does not help with that. For that we'd need to parse the whole YAML
  with libyaml. Maybe we'll do that in the future.

title: Resolving duplicates rows when requesting version
description:
Unless I'm drastically misunderstanding something, I think this is a bug. When resolving and refs contain a version, the resolution data frame unnests the versioned package dependency row into many rows (see reprex below). 

``` r
library(withr)
library(pkgdepends)

my_resolve <- function() {
  
  local_options(repos = list(CRAN = "https://cran.rstudio.com" ))
  tmp <- local_tempdir()
  
  prop <- new_pkg_installation_proposal(
    refs = "rlang@1.0.0",
    config = list(library = tmp)
  )
  
  prop$resolve()
  prop$get_resolution()
}

my_resolve()
#> ℹ Loading metadata database✔ Loading metadata database ... done
#> # A data frame: 10 × 31
#>    ref    type  direct directpkg status package version license needscompilation
#>    <chr>  <chr> <lgl>  <lgl>     <chr>  <chr>   <chr>   <chr>   <lgl>           
#>  1 rlang… stan… TRUE   TRUE      OK     rlang   1.0.0   MIT + … TRUE            
#>  2 rlang… stan… TRUE   TRUE      OK     rlang   1.0.0   MIT + … TRUE            
#>  3 rlang… stan… TRUE   TRUE      OK     rlang   1.0.0   MIT + … TRUE            
#>  4 rlang… stan… TRUE   TRUE      OK     rlang   1.0.0   MIT + … TRUE            
#>  5 rlang… stan… TRUE   TRUE      OK     rlang   1.0.0   MIT + … TRUE            
#>  6 rlang… stan… TRUE   TRUE      OK     rlang   1.0.0   MIT + … TRUE            
#>  7 rlang… stan… TRUE   TRUE      OK     rlang   1.0.0   MIT + … TRUE            
#>  8 rlang… stan… TRUE   TRUE      OK     rlang   1.0.0   MIT + … TRUE            
#>  9 rlang  stan… FALSE  TRUE      OK     rlang   1.1.4   MIT + … FALSE

#> #   filesize <int>, built <chr>, platform <chr>, rversion <chr>,

title: Installing a package from GitHub that depends on another GitHub repo
description:
Installing the package [Battenberg](https://github.com/Wedge-Oxford/battenberg/blob/master/DESCRIPTION), which depends on another repository called [ASCAT](https://github.com/VanLoo-lab), fails. The Battenberg [DESCRIPTION file](https://github.com/Wedge-Oxford/battenberg/blob/master/DESCRIPTION) only lists the dependency name, not its remote URL. Consequently, `pkgdepends` cannot locate the dependency and prevents the main package installation from completing.

Questions:

- **Ignore ASCAT dependency:** Is it possible to configure `pkgdepends` to ignore the ASCAT dependency during the Battenberg package installation?
- **Provide ASCAT source URL:** Can we provide the source URL for ASCAT to `pkgdepends` while installing Battenberg?

title: field names with difference in case trigger warning in make_installed_cache()
description:
If you have, for example, `readr` and `tidyverse` installed, you get this warning when running `new_pkg_deps()` (by default, I believe, only once every 8 hours due to `lifecycle` options)
``` r
library(pkgdepends)

pd <- new_pkg_deps("r-lib/pkgdepends")
#> Warning: The `x` argument of `as_tibble.matrix()` must have unique column names if `.name_repair` is omitted as of tibble 2.0.0.
#> Using compatibility `.name_repair`.
#> This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
#> Call `lifecycle::last_warnings()` to see where this warning was generated. 
```

because `readr` uses the field "Config/Needs/website" in its DESCRIPTION file
https://github.com/tidyverse/readr/blob/c9bc0e6cdeb7d8b777c188164e9d9d516efac163/DESCRIPTION#L68

while `tidyverse` uses the field "Config/Needs/Website" in its DESCRIPTION file
https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyverse/blob/195d8a45d7ac425bb29043ca418538753b79a1b8/DESCRIPTION#L63

so when the unique fields are made lowercase here in `pkgdepends:::make_installed_cache()`
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/blob/6b225ff9080bd079a4b04e71ad025e15c21bd329/R/type-installed.R#L71

the matrix `ret` ends up with duplicate colnames, which triggers the `tibble:::as_tibble.matrix()` warning because the method of resolving duplicate colnames has not been explicitly specified here
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/blob/6b225ff9080bd079a4b04e71ad025e15c21bd329/R/type-installed.R#L80

presumably it would be ideal to not end up with duplicate column names when building the `ret` matrix, but this warning could also be squelched by explicitly specifying the `.name_repair` argument of `tibble:::as_tibble()`

title: Libraries that depends each other will fails to solve
description:
Hi, I was trying to install packages with ```pak::pkg_install```, then I notice some packages failed to install.

This happens when we have two packages, A and B, and A depends on B, and B depends on A.

I think we all know R is not the best way to organize, conceptualize code, so there is some cases with some systems we can get things like that.

There is the argument "Split and create a new library", but there is several problems on that.

- Create a "utils" library that is used only to safe functions of non-related things just to be usable is pretty bad to organize and conceptualize
- Create a library by each function that is used by several packages causes to have a bunch of them! is a lot harder to maintain
- R does not have a way to organize more complex projects and their abstract
- R code does not needs to compile, which also means is not important the order in which the packages are installed (while they does not have a compilation that depends on a package)

The actual error is:
```R
Error:       
! error in pak subprocess
Caused by error in `select_next_task(state)`:
! Cannot select new package installation task.
ℹ 2 packages still waiting to install: rtestB and rtestA.
ℹ This is an internal error in pkgdepends, please report an issue at <https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/issues>.
Type .Last.error to see the more details.
```

Well, even with this there is still some concern about it, no idea if some packages with mutual dependence need to one be installed first, but while this is only on R code there should be no problem.

Thx!

title: Private git repositories (Azure Repos): cannot authenticate
description:
I can't handle private git repositories (in my case Azure Repos) that require authentication in the URL.

The Remote entry is something like: `git::https://dev.azure.com/org/project_git/package`.  

Starting e.g. from a `new_pkg_installation_proposal("git::https://dev.azure.com/org/project_git/package")`, {pkgdepends} retrieves the credentials using {gitcreds} from the system credential store, then builds the URL and should grab stuff from git.

Instead, I get an error from curl:

``` r
s_remote <- "git::https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/package"
p <- pkgdepends::new_pkg_installation_proposal(s_remote, config = list(library = tempfile()))
#> ℹ Creating library directory: 'C:\Users\LORENZ~1\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpM93Fz5\file4140718a10d'
p$resolve()
p$get_resolution()$error
#> [[1]]
#> <async_rejected/rlib_error_3_0/rlib_error/error>
#> Error in `value[[3L]](cond)`:
#> ! pkgdepends resolution error for
#> git::https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/package.
#> Caused by error: 
#> ! Failed to download 'DESCRIPTION' from git repo at
#> <https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/package>.
#> Caused by error in `(function (e) …`:
#> ! URL using bad/illegal format or missing URL
```

<sup>Created on 2023-05-24 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

By digging into the internals, I see that {pkgdepends} retrieves the username (in my org they have the form of `user@domain`), the password, and builds the resulting URL:
`https://user@domain:password@dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/package`

I believe that the @ in the username must be URL-encoded (`%40`) if using {pkgdepends}: I'm not sure if it's an Azure-specific pattern.   
I confirm it works by debugging into `pkgdepends:::async_git_list_refs_v2`.

I get the same behavior from the shell with the system git (notice that `user@` gets dropped):

```
git clone "https://user@domain:password@dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/package"
Cloning into 'rITAtools'...
fatal: unable to access 'https://domain:password@dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/package': URL using bad/illegal format or missing URL
```
Cloning succeeds with `git clone "https://user%40domain:password@dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/package"`.

It would be cool to be able to use the system git if available, as {remotes} already does.   
In that way, I can setup authentication in the `.gitconfig` with a PAT + HTTPS extra header (as [recommended](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/organizations/accounts/use-personal-access-tokens-to-authenticate?view=azure-devops&tabs=Windows#use-a-pat)), and that would avoid reimplementing a whole git client...

Thanks!

title: Solving for tree order in git fetch response
description:
I've been doing some more testing on how to get pkgdepends working with git repos hosted on Azure DevOps.

One problem I've encountered is that `unpack_packfile_repo()` is sensitive to the order in which the blobs/trees are received from the fetch request. The function is assuming that the root directory is the first tree it encounters.

In the case of Azure DevOps, the list that's received isn't guaranteed to have the root directory as the first tree in the list. The result is that `unpack_packfile_repo()` puts everything into the root directory of the output folder.

It might be possible to get the git server to provide the components in a particular order? I don't know enough about the protocol to say for sure. 

But even if it was, it seems more sensible to get the function to solve for the correct order in which to go through the trees/blobs. Perhaps generating the folder structure first and then writing out the blobs?

Sorry again that I don't have a reprex for you.

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/blob/9718c02b68a5437699be2b4da0d6244a3e662434/R/git-protocol.R#L507-L544

title: github remotes format partially incompatible with remotes package
description: If a dependency is hosted on GitHub, but its repository name doesn't match the package name, both `pkgdepends` and `remotes` allow explicitly specifying the package name. However, they are incompatible: `pkgdepends` expects a remote of the form `packagename=github::username/repo`, whereas `remotes` expects `github::packagename=username/repo`. This makes it impossible to both allow installation of one's package from GitHub with `remotes` and running a GitHub actions workflow that uses `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies` (which uses `pak` which uses `pkgdepends`)

title: not all .libPath() entries are taken into account when solving dependencies
description:
If `.libPath()` has several entries not all are evaluated during dependency lookup. This can lead to re-installation of already available packages.

title: Proper RSPM support
description:
* [x] Detect if a repo is RSPM. Once there is a response header for this, it'll be easy, until then we can do a GET to the `/status` API endpoint, then we'll also know the supported platforms.
* [x] Detect if the current platform is supported by RSPM. Supported platforms are listed at https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/__api__/status
* [x] Properly detect that RSPM packages are binaries. (For now we can detect that they _should be_ binaries, but unfortunately they aren't always. As soon as the `PACKAGES*` files have the information about binaries, we can do this properly.)
* [x] Detect if a downloaded package is a binary or not, from the the `x-package-type` header of the package download.
* [x] ~~Opt in to use RSPM automatically, via an env var or option.~~ Pretty easy already with `repo_add()`.
* [x] We could also use the Linux specific repo metadata, e.g. https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/latest/bin/linux/4.0-xenial/contrib/4.0/PACKAGES only lists the binary packages that are available for the `4.0-xenial` platform.

title: Run script before GitHub subdirectory is moved out of its context?
description:
In trying to remove some hacks from the nanoarrow package, which lives in a subdirectory of the https://github/apache/arrow-nanoarrow , I discovered that during the packaging phase the subdirectory is separated from the context before any script in the R package is run (e.g., `cleanup`). title: Installation error, new in recent pkgdepends
description:
Hi Gabor,

We've hit an issue installing packages with pkgdepends, somewhere between version 0.1.1 and 0.3.1 - MRE below:

```
tmp <- tempfile()
dir.create(tmp)
packages <- c("github::mrc-ide/naomi", "github::mrc-ide/first90release")
config <- list(library = tmp)
proposal <- pkgdepends::new_pkg_installation_proposal(packages, config,
                                                      policy = "lazy")
proposal$solve()
proposal$stop_for_solution_error()
proposal$download()
proposal$stop_for_download_error()
proposal$install()
```

this fails at the install step with

```
Error in done[[i]] : subscript out of bounds
> traceback()
6: do(m)
5: do(m)
4: do(i)
3: add_recursive_dependencies(plan)
2: install_package_plan(plan, lib = private$library, num_workers = nw, 
       cache = cache)
1: proposal$install()
```

I think this is probably the same error as https://github.com/r-lib/actions/issues/534 which you said there was a pak bug

Unfortunately we can't remove the Remotes fields from these packages - that's the suggestion on the other issue - as this is widespread across our cluster installation. We're going to try downgrading in the meantime though.

We did dig into the error and it's a bit of a mystery to us - the code around the error is old but looks like trying to mark "stringi" as done or not is causing the issue - perhaps some issue in how deps are being calculated? But I have no idea really sorry.

title: Output format for get_refs() changed, seems to break checkpoint logging
description:
Just recently I’ve [got reports](https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/checkpoint/issues/312) that the logging in checkpoint is broken, and on further investigation it appears to be because pkgdepends has changed how it returns config information.

My code is basically [as follows](https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/checkpoint/blob/748d407215d435e5353cbc8d4e63dbf4ae0df150/R/install_pkgs.R#L20-L21):

```r
inst <- pkgdepends::new_pkg_installation_proposal(pkgs, ...)
write_checkpoint_log(inst$get_refs())
```

Here `write_checkpoint` is a utility function that serialises the output of the various pkgdepends methods to json. IIRC, `get_refs()` used to return a data frame with assorted info. Now it returns a classed environment which can’t be serialised to json as-is.

I can work around this with some hacks, but I thought I’d ask what is the best way to save this config info to a file. The object contains functions which I guess I don’t want to serialise, and there may be other issues I’m not aware of. Should I forget about readable json and just save it as an rds file?

title: Further solver speedup
description:
- investigate rpicosat. It is R >= 3.4.0 currently, seemingly for no obvious reason: https://github.com/dirkschumacher/rpicosat/issues/4

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: Better workaround for the dll locking problem
description:
We can use `filelock::lock()` to try to acquire a lock on the DLL file. If this fails, that means that an R session (this one or another one) is using it. If it succeeds, then we get an exclusive lock on it, and other R sessions cannot load the package.

We need to be careful to avoid a deadlock, and always release locks immediately if we fail to acquire all of them.

Packages might have multiple dll files, and ideally we would lock all of them.

title: Handling of package dependency constraints ==, <= and <
description:
This is a follow-up of https://github.com/r-lib/remotes/issues/376 after having been referred to `pak` and as such indirectly also `pkgdepends`.

I'm considering the following "artificial" package `testdeps`:
```
Type: Package
Package: testdeps
Title: Handling Package Dependency Specification
Version: 0.0.1
Authors@R: person("Martin", "Studer", "martin.remo.studer@gmail.com", c("aut", "cre"))
Description: Testing handling of package dependency specifications.
License: MIT
Imports: 
    abind,
    biogas (>= 1.9.0),
    coop (> 0.4-0),
    deal (== 1.2-35),
    effsize (<= 0.7.0),
    face (< 0.1-4)
```

I have an environment established as follows:
```
install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("r-lib/pkgdepends")

dir.create("libdir1")
.libPaths(c("libdir1", .libPaths()))

remotes::install_version("biogas", "1.8.0")
remotes::install_version("coop", "0.4-0")
remotes::install_version("deal", "1.2-37")
remotes::install_version("effsize", "0.7.1")
remotes::install_version("face", "0.1-5")

dir.create("libdir2")
.libPaths(c("libdir2", .libPaths()))
```
* A `.libPaths()` in the order `libdir2`, `libdir1`, ...
* `libdir1` contains some of the package dependencies but with versions not matching the constraints of `testdeps` - of special interest are the dependencies `deal`, `effsize` and `face` which use dependency constraints `==`, `<=` and `<`
* `libdir2` is an empty library directory at the top of `.libPaths()`

I now use `pkgdepends` to attempt to solve the dependencies for `testdeps` in the following way:
```
r <- pkgdepends::remotes()$new("deps::.", library = .libPaths()[1])
r$solve(policy = "lazy")
```
* above `DESCRIPTION` file present in current working directory
* using `.libPaths()[1]`, i.e. `libdir2` as the library directory

This results in the following output:
```
ℹ Checking for package metadata updates
✔ All 6 metadata files are current.                                             
✔ Loading session disk cached package metadata                                  
✔ Using cached package metadata                                                 
PKG FAILED SOLUTION, 0 refs, resolved in 85ms, solved in 19ms ─────────────────
  * Cannot install `deps::.`.
    - Cannot install dependency deal
  * Cannot install `deps::.`.
    - Cannot install dependency effsize
  * Cannot install `deps::.`.
    - Cannot install dependency face
```
I would have expected this to give a solution since `libdir2` is empty and it is theoretically possible for `deal`, `effsize` and `face` to be installed with appropriate versions without affecting any existing installations of those packages (which are installed in `libdir1`). A failure seems reasonable if package installation would result in loss of existing installations but that's not the case in this example.

title: `pkg_deps_tree()`: Circular dependencies with Remotes cause error
description:
We have a "soft" circular dependency, where shiny suggests shinytest, and shinytest imports shiny. They each list the other in the `Remotes:` field, since we're using dev versions from github. This causes an error in our CI workflow:

title: How to suppress progress reporting when knitting?
description:
I tried to make a reprex that called `pd$solve()` and struggled to suppress the progress reporting. Seems like that should be automatic when knitting?

FWIW `rlang::is_interactive()` consults the `knitr.in.progress` option:

https://github.com/r-lib/rlang/blob/4513283d8640275e53d232af02ef342abaf3870c/R/state.R#L121

 @gaborcsardi suggested using the `pkg.show_progress` option, but that didn't actually suppress the progress reporting.

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/blob/c6617afa7d36e26bfcf7f70fd39e4c786820afaf/R/download-progress-bar.R#L256

Here's the actual example, with the solution we settled on for now (`suppressMessages()`).

``` r
# devtools::install_github("r-lib/pkgdepends")
library(pkgdepends)
library(gert)
#> Linking to libgit2 v1.0.1, ssh support: YES
#> Global config: /Users/jenny/.gitconfig
#> Default user: Jenny Bryan <jenny.f.bryan@gmail.com>

# should work but doesn't currently
# options(pkg.show_progress = FALSE)

f <- function() {
  pd <- new_pkg_deps("local::.")
  suppressMessages(pd$solve())
  dat <- pd$get_resolution()
  sort(unique(dat$ref))
}

git_branch_checkout("inline-rematch2")
#> <git repository>: /Users/jenny/rrr/usethis[@inline-rematch2]
deps_now <- f()
length(deps_now)
#> [1] 33

git_branch_checkout("master")
#> <git repository>: /Users/jenny/rrr/usethis[@master]
deps_then <- f()
length(deps_then)
#> [1] 41

setdiff(deps_then, deps_now)
#> [1] "digest"    "ellipsis"  "pillar"    "pkgconfig" "rematch2"  "tibble"   
#> [7] "utf8"      "vctrs"
```

title: Installation order may be wrong
description:
Consider this situation:
- pkgdepends depends on callr, 
- callr depends on processx,
- callr is installed from binary
- pkgdepends and callr are installed from source
- callr gets installed first, potentially, because it is a binary
- then pkgdepends starts building both processx and pkgdepends at the same time, missing the fact that processx is a (recursive) dependency of pkgdepends.

The solution could be to add the transitive edges to the dependency graph. This will make the graph quite dense, but hopefully that's OK.

description:
Something that appeared while testing checkpoint. If I use a snapshot that's old enough that there is no package binary available, it fails. Perhaps in this case, there should be a fallback to the source version, mimicking the behaviour of `install.packages`.

Example:

```
r$> pkgcache::pkg_cache_delete_files()

    inst <- new_pkg_installation_proposal(
        "R6",

Here, I'm using R 3.6.2, and the MRAN snapshot doesn't have binaries for that (only 3.5). title: Suggestion: allow manually setting no. of install workers
description:
Currently, `ps::ps_cpu_count()` [returns NA on Win 10](https://github.com/r-lib/ps/issues/77), as does `getOption("Ncpus")`. This means that `new_pkg_installation_proposal$install()` will default to using only one worker. Until the core detection is working, consider allowing the no. of workers to be set in the `install` call, so that parallel installs can be carried out on Windows.

It goes the other way too: if you're installing packages that require compiling C++ code, you may not want to have lots of them running in parallel. In this situation, reducing the no. of workers would be a way to reduce the chances of running out of memory.

title: Caching confusion with multiple package versions
description:
Related to https://github.com/r-lib/pkgcache/issues/39. I thought at first that pkgcache can't handle multiple package versions, but it appears that it does. However, I'm finding that downloading and/or installing multiple versions can screw up.

Here, I attempt to install tibble first from the MRAN snapshot for 2020-03-01, and then from 2019-03-01. I deleted the R-pkg dir first to ensure that the cache was clean.

```r
inst <- new_pkg_installation_proposal(
    "tibble",
    config=list(`cran-mirror`="https://mran.microsoft.com/snapshot/2020-03-01",
                library="~/tibble2020")
)
inst$resolve()
inst$solve()
inst$download()
inst$install()
```
```r
inst2 <- new_pkg_installation_proposal(
    "tibble",
    config=list(`cran-mirror`="https://mran.microsoft.com/snapshot/2019-03-01",
                library="~/tibble2019")
)
inst2$resolve()
inst2$solve()
inst2$download()
inst2$install()
```

Afterwards, the installed version of tibble is the same in both directories:

```
r$> grep("^Version",
         readLines(system.file("DESCRIPTION", package="tibble", lib.loc="~/tibble2020")), value=TRUE)
[1] "Version: 2.1.3"

r$> grep("^Version",
         readLines(system.file("DESCRIPTION", package="tibble", lib.loc="~/tibble2019")), value=TRUE)
[1] "Version: 2.1.3"
r$>
```

If you go to the MRAN snapshot sites, you'll see that the correct tibble version at [2019-03-01](https://cran.microsoft.com/snapshot/2019-03-01/web/packages/tibble/) was 2.0.1.

title: new_pkg_installation_proposal$install fails with config dependencies=pkg_dep_types()

library(pkgdepends)
unlink("~/newlib", recursive=TRUE)
inst <- new_pkg_installation_proposal(c("knitr", "cli", "testthat", "mockery", "darts"),
    config=list(library="~/newlib", dependencies=pkg_dep_types()))
inst$resolve()
inst$solve()
inst$download()
inst$install()
```

Result should be only darts is installed in ~/newlib, and nothing else. If I remove `dependencies` from the config list, then everything is installed.

title: Check pkgman compatibility for resolution v2
Re-add metadata support
description:
Need these for devtools compatibility:

- RemoteType (all)
- RemoteRef (all)
- RemoteRepos (cran)
- RemoteSha (cran (version), local, bitbucket, git, bioc, svn, github)
- RemotePkgType  (cran)
- RemoteUrl (local, git, bioc, svn)
- RemoteUsername (local if uses GH, bitbucket, github)
- RemoteRepo (local if uses GH, bitbucket, github)
- RemoteBranch (local if uses git)
- RemoteSubdir (bitbucket, git, github)
- RemoteSvnSubdir (svn)
- RemoteRevision (svn)
- RemoteArgs (svn)
- RemoteHost (github)
- RemoteMirror (bioc)
- RemoteRelease (bioc)
- RemoteUsername (bioc)
- RemotePassword (bioc)
- RemoteRevision (bioc)
- RemoteSha (bioc)
- GithubRepo (github)
- GithubUsername (github)
- GithubRef (github)
- GithubSHA1 (github)
- GithubSubdir (github)

So we have these:

- [x] cran: 
   - RemoteRef
   - RemoteType
   - RemoteRepos
   - RemoteSha (version number, really)
   - RemotePkgType
- [x] bioc:
   - RemoteRef
   - RemoteType
   - RemoteRepos
   - RemoteSha (version number)
   - RemotePkgType
- [x] standard:
   - RemoteRef
   - RemoteType
   - RemoteRepos
   - RemoteSha (version number)
   - RemotePkgType
- [x] local:
   - RemoteRef
   - RemoteType
   - RemoteSha
   - RemoteUrl
   - RemoteUsername (if GH)
   - RemoteRepo (if GH)
   - RemoteBranch (if git)
- [x] github
   - RemoteType
   - RemoteRef
   - RemoteSha
   - RemoteUsername
   - RemoteRepo
   - RemoteSubdir
   - RemoteHost
   - GithubRepo
   - GithubUsername
   - GithubRef
   - GithubSHA1
   - GithubSubdir

title: Refactor resolution
description:
To allow a lightweight API to define new remote types.

Also, make use the metadata cache, to get rid of the complicated procedure for cran, bioc and standard packages.

title: Resolve standard packages in batches, for speedup.
Sometimes packages are not cached
description:
Need to investigate why.

```
❯ r <- remotes$new("r-lib/usethis"); r$resolve(); r$download_resolution()
→ Updating CRAN metadata
✔ CRAN metadata current

→ Updating CRAN metadata

title: Fast resolution sub-optimal
description: We need to look at the binaries as well, if the false resolution comes from a source package. Because otherwise all of its dependencies will be installed from source packages as well....

title: Refactor the resolution progress bar and related async HTTP.
description: We need to follow individual HTTP requests to get a better picture of what is going on.

title: Better metadata cache
description:
Have a cached format that is very easy to resolve. I.e. pre-compute the fields that are needed for
resolution.

title: Tree drawing from the solution, optionally
description:
Solution makes more sense, since that has a single version for each package, and we can also annotate it nicely:

- [ ] status: installed, need to download, in cache, need to build, etc.
- [x] version
- [ ] bytes to download
- [x] directly or indirectly required

???

title: `installed` remotes do not need `LinkingTo`
description: Interestingly, "LinkingTo" is not in the macOS binary PACKAGES file, but it is in the Windows binary PACKAGES file. I wonder if this is intentional.

title: lpSolve is slow for the new LP problem
description: We need to use another solver, like glpk. glpk has R packages, `Rglpk` might do it.

title: When resolving, check if package needs compilation
description: This can be used during the installation, e.g. to check for rtools / build tools. CRAN / BioC packages declare this in the `NeedsCompilation` field. GH / local packages can just check if there is a `src`  directory. installed packages do not need compilation.

title: Consolidate print methods
description: For all of the `pkg*` tools. Even within `pkgdepends` they are inconsistent. We could use some higher level CLI tools....

title: Support updating packages
description: I.e. prefer newer versions in `solve()`.

title: Print a log message for starting to build a package
description: I.e. `progress_bar$log(...)`...

title: Solution bug: we do not need all packages, actually
description:
E.g. is something is required only by a CRAN version, but that version won't be installed, because another one is preferred, then we don't need it. 

So we need to change the LP problem, slightly. We only require direct refs and their dependencies.

title: Do not build vignettes for GH packages when downloading solution
description:
But do build them when downloading a resolution. I.e. build them for `repoman`, but not for `pkgman`.

From https://github.com/r-lib/pkgman/issues/37

title: Do not HEAD CRAN source packages
description: Or GH packages with the correct SHA.

title: Better error message if `solve()` fails
description: See #69 for an example.

title: Handle recommended packages specially
description: Right now we are trying to install them into the target library, which is probably not good.

title: User-Agent for downloads
description:
Include:
- R version
- whether it is a direct dl or a dependency
- dependency of which package (?)

title: `remotes` print method could do something meaningful
Explain a solve() failure
description: What conflicts prevent the installation of a package?

title: Improve progress bar
description: We need to follow the download progress of each package individually. There is no other way to have a sensible progress bar afaict.

title: Check on earlier R versions
description: i.e. `use_tidy_ci()`

title: direct refs are not marked properly in (re)solution output if they are already installed
installed packages are not checked for fast resolution dependencies
description: Because we only check them when adding fast refs. Rather, we need to to check them at the end of the fast resolution.

title: download_solution fails if no downloads needed
Fast resolution needs to consider CRAN & BioC together
description: Because the BioC package might depend on CRAN packages, which might depend on BioC packages, etc.

description: Right now the `file` column of a installation plan is set to a cache directory/NA, e.g. `"/var/folders/dt/r5s12t392tb5sk181j3gs4zw0000gn/T//Rtmp923JLv/filea46714824832/NA"`. It would be more informative if this was the path the package was installed to.

title: fix bug for multiple versions of the same package in a CRAN or Bioc repo
description: Currently only the first version is added, and a warning is printed. All versions should be added, and we select based on platform and R version requirements, defaulting to the latest version.

title: Better automatic cache location.
description: Currently you need to supply the cache directory where the packages are downloaded, the default is a temporary directory. This is probably wrong, and we need an OS specific location, in the user’s cache dir. But this is tricky, because multiple `pkgdepends` instances might be running at the same time. For the package files, this is not a problem, but we need to coordinate caching the CRAN (etc) metadata, so that a resolution is consistent, i.e. the same metadata is used for everything.

description: When I do `pkgman::pkg_install("rstudio/rmarkdown")` there's a noticeable delay between pressing enter and seeing `✔ Resolving dependencies`. Could we get an interim spinner there? (Or maybe just move the message earlier?)

title: Error in returning the solution for dplyr
description:
The original error (same as in the reproducible example below) by running
```r
r <- pkgdepends::remotes$new("dplyr", library = .libPaths()[[1]])
r$solve()
```

This seems somewhat particular to my library (it works fine for `library = tempdir()`), but I have saved the intermediate resolution object (obtained at https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/blob/92aceb05522f7b7703c22e6b5dce3882d6a35ad9/R/resolution.R#L147 as an RDS. [dplyr.rds.gz](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/files/1438272/dplyr.rds.gz) (I had to gzip it so github would accept the file)

```r
resolution <- readRDS("dplyr.rds")

getf <- function(f) {
  unlist(lapply(resolution, function(x) vcapply(x$files, "[[", f)))
}

getf("target")
#> Error in vapply(X, FUN, FUN.VALUE = character(1), ...) :
#>   values must be length 1,
#>  but FUN(X[[1]]) result is length 0

title: Consider local packages
description:
I.e. if a package is already installed locally, we don't need to download it.

Optionally, because for `repoman` we do want to download it.

title: Should use `pkgbuild` to build the package
More general package cache
description: It could just support arbitrary fields. E.g. GH remotes would need user, repo, sha, etc., local remotes maybe a file modification date and/or md5, etc.

title: Speed up CRAN metadata cache
description: Keep it in memory.

title: Solving an installation
description:
I.e. take the resolution for the packages, and the already installed packages, and work out what exactly needs to be downloaded and installed.

This is a discrete optimization problem, linear programming, probably. These rules must hold:

1. All dependency versions need to be satisfied.
2. For each package we need to have exactly one version.
3. For directly specified versions (and refs) we need exactly those.

These rules are to select exactly one solution, if multiple solutions satisfy the previous criteria:

4. Already installed packages are preferred to packages that need to be downloaded.
5. Binary packages are preferred to source packages.

We ignore base packages completely, and we also ignore recommended packages if they are installed in the system packages library.

This optimization problem corresponds to the default configuration. Alternative ones will be considered as well, e.g. to upgrade old packages to their newest available versions.

@jimhester Feedback welcome!

title: NEed to resolve the installed packages as well
description:
To make sure that their correct dependencies are installed.

We can do this as a separate step after the resolution, or in parallel with that.

title: Dependencies from the calculated resolution
description: For one or more packages.

title: Syntax for remotes where repo name / file name if different from package name.
description:
cc @jimhester 

To make dependency resolution easier. 

We could put the optional package name to the front or the end of the string, maybe front is better. We also need a new separator for it. How about a single `:`? If there is no `:` then the package name must match the repo name or file name (for `url` or `local` remotes).

```
package:user/repo
package:github::user/repo
package:url::https://xy.com/filename_1.0.0.tar.gz
```

Another alternative to `:` is `=`. We could also change the order of the remote type and the package name, I don't mind:
```
package:user/repo
github::package:user/repo
url::package:https://xy.com/filename_1.0.0.tar.gz
```

It does not look very good, but this syntax should be rarely needed, anyway.

This is the current GitHub remote syntax: 
```r
    github = paste0(
      "^",
      ## Optional remote type
      "(?:github::)?",
      ## Username
      "(?<username>(?:[^/]+))/",
      ## Repo
      "(?<repo>[^/@#]+)",
      ## Subdirectory
      "(?:/(?<subdir>(?:[^@#]*[^@#/])/?))?",
      ## Commit / PR / Release
      github_detail,
      "$"
    )
```

where

```r
  github_commitish_rx <- "(?:@(?<commitish>[^*].*))"
  github_pull_rx <- "(?:#(?<pull>[0-9]+))"
  github_release_rx <- "(?:@(?<release>[*]release))"
  github_detail <- sprintf(
    "(?:(?:%s)|(?:%s)|(?:%s))?",
    github_commitish_rx,
    github_pull_rx,
    github_release_rx
  )
```
